name: websec
label: Web security testing

tools.name: nuclei
tools.use: Template-driven vulnerability scanning — thousands of checks for known CVEs, misconfigurations and exposures. Templates are baked in at /opt/ghost/nuclei-templates.
tools.args: -u URL for one target or -l HOSTS.txt for many; -t /opt/ghost/nuclei-templates points at the baked templates and -duc skips the update check. -severity high,critical narrows, -je FILE exports JSON.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.use: Fuzz anything in a request from a wordlist — paths, parameters, virtual hosts — matching on status, size or words.
tools.args: -w WORDLIST -u URL with FUZZ where the wordlist goes. -mc 200,301 matches status codes, -fs N filters a response size, -H 'Header: v' adds a header. Wordlists live under /opt/ghost/wordlists.

tools.name: gobuster
tools.use: Brute directories, DNS subdomains or virtual hosts.
tools.args: A mode — dir, dns or vhost — then -w WORDLIST and -u URL (dir/vhost) or -d DOMAIN (dns).

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.use: Detect and confirm SQL injection end to end — enumerate databases, dump tables, read files. --batch runs unattended.
tools.args: -u URL with the parameter to test, or -r REQUEST.txt for a saved request. --batch answers prompts with defaults, --dbs lists databases, --dump pulls a table, --level/--risk raise coverage.

tools.name: dalfox
tools.use: Detect and confirm XSS — parameter analysis, payload firing and verification.
tools.args: A mode — url, file or pipe — then the target. `url URL` scans one URL; --custom-payload FILE adds payloads, -o FILE writes results.

tools.name: commix
tools.use: Detect and confirm command injection. --batch runs unattended.
tools.args: -u URL with the injectable parameter, or -r REQUEST.txt. --batch runs unattended; --os-cmd 'id' runs one command instead of opening a shell.

tools.name: nikto
tools.use: Scan a web server for dangerous files, outdated software and misconfigurations.
tools.args: -h URL or host. -p PORT sets a non-default port, -o FILE -Format txt writes a report, -Tuning selects test classes.

tools.name: wafw00f
tools.use: Fingerprint the WAF in front of a target before you choose payloads.
tools.args: One or more URLs. -a tests every signature instead of stopping at the first match, -o FILE writes the result.

tools.name: arjun
tools.use: Discover hidden HTTP parameters a form or endpoint accepts but does not advertise.
tools.args: -u URL to probe. -m GET|POST|JSON sets the method, -oT FILE writes the parameters found, -w WORDLIST uses a custom parameter list.

tools.name: hydra
tools.use: Online login testing across many protocols — http-post-form, http-get (basic), ssh, ftp. The core credential-testing tool.
tools.args: Credentials, then host, then service: -l USER (or -L USERS.txt), -p PASS (or -P PASSWORDS.txt), the host, and a module like http-post-form with its "path:body:fail" string, ssh or ftp. Lists live under /opt/ghost/wordlists.

tools.name: john
tools.use: John the Ripper — recover passwords from hashes you have obtained, offline.
tools.args: A file of hashes. --wordlist=FILE runs a dictionary attack, --format=NAME sets the hash type, --show prints what has been recovered.

tools.name: jwt_tool
tools.use: Analyse and test JSON Web Tokens — alg confusion, none, weak-secret cracking, claim tampering (auth testing).
tools.args: The token, then a mode: -T tampers interactively, -X a runs the alg-confusion/none checks, -C -d WORDLIST cracks a weak secret.

tools.name: curl
tools.use: Craft any HTTP request by hand — headers, methods, cookies, bodies — to reproduce or refine a finding.
tools.args: The URL and whatever the request needs — -X METHOD, -H 'Header: v', -d BODY, -b 'cookie=v', -i to include response headers, -k to skip TLS verification.

tools.name: openssl
tools.use: Inspect TLS, and the everyday crypto odd jobs: hashes, base64, hex, random bytes.
tools.args: s_client -connect HOST:443 -servername HOST reads a live certificate. Local forms take no network: dgst -sha256 FILE, base64 -d, rand -hex 16, enc for symmetric crypto.

tools.name: python3
tools.use: Write a custom request or check script when the tools cannot express it. requests is installed.
tools.args: -c and a program, or a script path.

tools.name: jq
tools.use: Filter and reshape JSON — API responses, nuclei -json output.
tools.args: A jq filter, then a file — or nothing after it to read stdin.

tools.name: rg
tools.use: Search inside the output and reproductions you have written to the workspace.
tools.args: A pattern and a path, relative to the workspace. -n prints line numbers, -i ignores case.

notes: For authorized web security testing only. This box has network access and every tool here acts against the target — it sends real payloads and tests logins, so its traffic is attributable to this machine and must only run against systems you are permitted to test. Work in stages and write each to the workspace: discover content and parameters (ffuf, gobuster, arjun), sweep for known issues (nuclei -t /opt/ghost/nuclei-templates -duc, nikto), then confirm a finding by demonstrating it (sqlmap --batch, dalfox, commix --batch) and test authentication (hydra for online login testing, jwt_tool for token attacks, john for offline recovery). Wordlists are baked at /opt/ghost/wordlists (common.txt, raft-medium-directories.txt, top-usernames-shortlist.txt, top-10000-passwords.txt). Write each confirmed finding with its reproduction — the exact request or command — to the workspace rather than only reporting it inline. Output too large to return inline is kept under /run/ghost-runs/ — reach it with a shell command, not the file tools.
